faqs.q: What is the MannTek CBC-C cable-release cryogenic breakaway coupling used for?
faqs.a: The CBC-C is a cable-release breakaway coupling that protects LNG and liquid-gas hose assemblies against excessive load, releasing a clamp when a cable pulls instead of breaking bolts. MannTek recommends it for systems with a high operating pressure and a weak piping structure; see the [LNG and cryogenic couplings shelf](/c/lng-cryogenic-couplings).

faqs.q: How do I read the MannTek CBC-C part numbers?
faqs.a: In the rows IH-MNT-CBCC-050, -063, -080, -100 and -150 are the CBC-C in DN 50, DN 63, DN 80, DN 100 and DN 150. The last three digits are the nominal size in DN.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the MannTek CBC-C come in?
faqs.a: Five sizes are listed: DN 50, DN 63, DN 80, DN 100 and DN 150. MannTek's product page gives 2" to 8" for the cable release type, so ask if you need a size that is not listed.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature is the MannTek CBC-C rated for?
faqs.a: MannTek gives a working pressure of 25 bar and a service temperature down to -196 °C. The body is stainless steel and the seals are PTFE.

faqs.q: How does the MannTek CBC-C release?
faqs.a: It has a clamp system and an external collar with an attached cable. When the cable pulls, the clamp releases; both halves have their own valve and both valves close immediately after an emergency disconnection, so the line is shut off on both sides of the break.

faqs.q: When should I choose the CBC-C rather than the breaking-bolt CBC or the PERC?
faqs.a: Choose the breaking-bolt CBC where the line and its supports can carry the release force, the CBC-C where they cannot or where the release is triggered by cable from a fixed point. And the PERC where the release must also be triggered remotely by the emergency shutdown system.

faqs.q: What connections does the MannTek CBC-C take?
faqs.a: Inlet and outlet connections are chosen individually: thread, flange or hose shank. Send the size, the connections, the medium and line pressure, and say where the release cable will be anchored.

faqs.q: Is the CBC-C suitable for liquid nitrogen as well as LNG?
faqs.a: It is built for LNG and liquid-gas hose assemblies down to -196 °C, so it also suits other cryogenic liquefied gases such as nitrogen. Confirm the medium on your request so we check the seals and body.

We confirm the specification and lead time on the quotation; start on [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: How does the CBC-C compare with the breaking-bolt CBC?
faqs.a: The CBC-C releases by cable and clamp in five sizes from DN 50 to DN 150, while the [breaking-bolt CBC](/p/manntek-cbc-cryogenic-breakaway-coupling-breaking-bolt) breaks bolts at a calculated load and is listed from DN 25 to DN 200 in industrial and marine versions.

faqs.q: What is the MannTek CBC breaking-bolt cryogenic breakaway coupling used for?
faqs.a: The MannTek CBC protects an LNG or liquid-gas transfer line against drive-aways and pull-aways at terminals and loading points. It is the weakest link in the hose line or loading arm: when the pull reaches a defined force the bolts break, the coupling separates and the poppet valves in both halves close; see the [LNG and cryogenic couplings shelf](/c/lng-cryogenic-couplings).

faqs.q: How do I read the MannTek CBC part numbers?
faqs.a: In the rows IH-MNT-CBC-I-050 is the industrial version in DN 50 and IH-MNT-CBC-M-050 is the marine version, with the last three digits the DN size from 025 to 200. The listing has 14 part numbers.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the MannTek CBC come in?
faqs.a: DN 25 (1") to DN 200 (8") in industrial and marine versions, 14 part numbers. MannTek publishes flow capacity from 460 L/min at DN 25 to 24,200 L/min at DN 200.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature is the MannTek CBC rated for?
faqs.a: MannTek gives a working pressure of 25 bar and a service temperature down to -196 °C. The body is stainless steel with engineered PTFE seals and a poppet valve design.

faqs.q: Industrial or marine MannTek CBC: which version do I need?
faqs.a: The industrial version releases at any pull angle from 0 to 90°, installed to at least one fixed point. While the marine version releases on straight axial pull only and resists torsion and bending to prevent unwanted separation between two hose strings.

faqs.q: How is the breaking load of the MannTek CBC set?
faqs.a: MannTek calculates the breaking load for each installation. Send the hose size and length, the operating pressure, the medium and how the line is fixed; the breaking force is less dependent on line pressure, according to MannTek.

faqs.q: What connections does the MannTek CBC take?
faqs.a: Inlet and outlet are chosen individually: female or male NPT thread, flanges to EN, ANSI, TW or TTMA, or an integrated hose shank, so no nipples or reducers are needed.

faqs.q: What happens after the MannTek CBC releases?
faqs.a: Both halves close their valves as they separate, so the product stays in the hose and the pipe, and one person can reset the coupling on site in minutes without special tools. It is passive, needs no external power and has no loose parts to lose.

faqs.q: What is the MannTek DCC hose unit used for?
faqs.a: The DCC hose unit is the moving half of a MannTek Dry Cryogenic Coupling, with an integrated swivel and handles, fitted to hose assemblies and loading arms for temporary connection between a storage tank and a mobile transport unit. See the [LNG and cryogenic couplings shelf](/c/lng-cryogenic-couplings). Push and turn opens the valves in both halves.

faqs.q: How do I read the MannTek DCC hose unit part numbers?
faqs.a: IH-MNT-DCC-HU-050 is the hose unit (HU) in DN 50 to the ISO/TS 18683 interface, and IH-MNT-DCC-HU-ISO-050 is the same size to the ISO 21593 interface. The last three digits are the DN size, 13 part numbers in all.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the MannTek DCC hose unit come in?
faqs.a: Six sizes in the ISO/TS 18683 version, DN 25 to DN 150, and seven in the ISO 21593 version, DN 25 to DN 200 (1" to 8"). MannTek publishes flow capacity from 250 L/min at 1" to 24,000 L/min at 8".

faqs.q: What temperature and pressure applies to the MannTek DCC?
faqs.a: The service temperature is down to -196 °C, and the working pressure is confirmed with the quotation. MannTek reports more than 10,000 connect and disconnect cycles in cryogenic testing.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the DCC and the DCC ISO?
faqs.a: The DCC follows ISO/TS 18683 (ASTM F3312) in DN 25 to DN 150 and suits existing installations and most land-based LNG work. The DCC ISO follows ISO 21593 in 1" to 8", the standard for dry couplings in ship-to-ship LNG bunkering.

faqs.q: Which gases can the MannTek DCC handle?
faqs.a: MannTek designs the DCC for cryogenic liquefied gases (LNG, nitrogen, oxygen, argon and ethylene) down to -196 °C. It needs no retightening during the cool-down phase.

faqs.q: What connections and options does the MannTek DCC hose unit have?
faqs.a: NPT thread or ANSI or EN flange, with sockets from Ø 56 mm (1") to Ø 238 mm (6"). Options include colour coding and a stop-before-disconnect function that blocks separation if a valve fails to seal.

faqs.q: Does the MannTek DCC need retightening as it cools down?
faqs.a: No. Unlike a flanged or threaded joint, it needs no retightening during the cool-down phase, because it uses the bayonet principle and self-sealing valve design of MannTek's Dry Disconnect Couplings.

We confirm the specification and lead time on the quotation; start on [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: How does the DCC hose unit differ from the DCC tank unit?
faqs.a: The hose unit has an integrated swivel and handles and is the moving half on the hose, while the [tank unit](/p/manntek-dcc-dry-cryogenic-coupling-tank-unit) is the fixed half with no swivel, mounted on the tank, tank truck, rail tanker or ship manifold.

faqs.q: What is the MannTek DCC tank unit used for?
faqs.a: The DCC tank unit is the fixed half of a MannTek Dry Cryogenic Coupling, with no swivel, mounted as the filling or discharge connector on cryogenic storage tanks, tank trucks, rail tankers, containers and ship bunker manifolds. See the [LNG and cryogenic couplings shelf](/c/lng-cryogenic-couplings). A DCC hose unit couples to it with a turning motion.

faqs.q: How do I read the MannTek DCC tank unit part numbers?
faqs.a: IH-MNT-DCC-TU-050 is the tank unit (TU) in DN 50 to the ISO/TS 18683 interface, and IH-MNT-DCC-TU-ISO-050 is the same size to the ISO 21593 interface. The last three digits are the DN size, 13 part numbers in all.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the MannTek DCC tank unit come in?
faqs.a: Six sizes to ISO/TS 18683, DN 25 to DN 150, and seven to ISO 21593, DN 25 to DN 200 (1" to 8"). MannTek publishes flow capacity from 250 L/min at 1" to 24,000 L/min at 8".

faqs.q: What temperature and pressure applies to the MannTek DCC tank unit?
faqs.a: The service temperature is down to -196 °C and the working pressure is confirmed for the size and build with the quotation. The body is stainless steel with PTFE seals.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the DCC and the DCC ISO tank unit?
faqs.a: The DCC follows ISO/TS 18683 (ASTM F3312) in DN 25 to DN 150, while the DCC ISO follows ISO 21593 in 1" to 8", the standard for ship-to-ship LNG bunkering. Choose the one that matches the other half.

faqs.q: Will a MannTek DCC connect to a coupling from another maker?
faqs.a: Only if the other coupling follows the same interface: ISO/TS 18683 for the DCC and ISO 21593 for the DCC ISO. Choose the one that matches the other half, or the standard your terminal or vessel specifies.

faqs.q: Where is the MannTek DCC tank unit mounted?
faqs.a: As the filling or discharge connector on cryogenic storage tanks, tank trucks, rail tankers, containers and ship bunker manifolds. Connections are NPT thread or ANSI or EN flange.

faqs.q: What options does the MannTek DCC tank unit have?

faqs.q: What is the MannTek PERC powered emergency release coupling used for?
faqs.a: The MannTek PERC is a breakaway coupling for LNG transfer that can also be released on command. It uses the breaking-bolt design of MannTek's cryogenic breakaways and adds a chamber, isolated from the transferred medium, into which high-pressure nitrogen is injected to release the coupling; see the [LNG and cryogenic couplings shelf](/c/lng-cryogenic-couplings).

faqs.q: How do I read the MannTek PERC part numbers?
faqs.a: IH-MNT-PERC-065 is the PERC in DN 65 (2-1/2"), and -080, -100, -150 and -200 are DN 80, DN 100, DN 150 and DN 200. The last three digits are the DN size, five part numbers in all.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the MannTek PERC come in?
faqs.a: 2-1/2" (DN 65) to 8" (DN 200), with female or male NPT thread or EN, ANSI, TW or TTMA flanges. MannTek publishes flow capacity from 2,800 L/min at 2-1/2" to 24,200 L/min at 8".

faqs.q: What are the three ways to release the MannTek PERC?
faqs.a: By an ESD signal from the ship or shore emergency shutdown system, by manual override independent of the electrical signal, and passively by breaking bolts designed to be the weakest point. If power is lost the PERC still works as a passive breakaway coupling.

faqs.q: What controls the MannTek PERC?
faqs.a: MannTek's HPN2 high-pressure nitrogen unit holds the control, monitoring and release system. Its PLC is programmed for each application under third-party supervision, and MannTek states its SIL2 PLC LNG transfer systems have been assessed by DNV-GL against IEC 61508 and IEC 61511.

faqs.q: Is the MannTek PERC SIL rated?
faqs.a: MannTek states that its SIL2 PLC LNG transfer systems have been assessed by DNV-GL and declared compliant to SIL2, developed in accordance with IEC 61508 and IEC 61511. Ask for the documents that apply to your system.

faqs.q: Where is the MannTek PERC used?
faqs.a: On LNG bunkering ship-to-ship, shore-to-ship and truck-to-ship, and LNG cargo transfer. MannTek also lists the PERC for ammonia, methanol and carbon capture transfer systems.

faqs.q: What is a vessel separation device on a PERC system?
faqs.a: A VSD can feed the PERC: two wires shorter than the hose trip VSD 1, which signals ESD 1 to stop pumps and close ESD valves, and then VSD 2, which signals ESD 2 and releases the PERC through the HPN2 unit.

faqs.a: The PERC adds a nitrogen release on command on top of the breaking-bolt backup, in five sizes from DN 65 to DN 200, while the [CBC](/p/manntek-cbc-cryogenic-breakaway-coupling-breaking-bolt) is purely passive and goes from DN 25 to DN 200.
